build an rpg and farming simulator: Farming & Animal Husbandry

​Crops: Planting, watering, and harvesting seasonal crops (e.g., strawberries in Spring, blueberries in Summer, pumpkins in Fall).

​Livestock: Raising chickens, ducks, cows, goats, and pigs. Animals produce goods that can be converted into artisan products (like turning milk into cheese or truffles into truffle oil).

​Farm Types: At the start, you choose a farm layout tailored to different playstyles-from classic agricultural plots to riverland fishing spots or wilderness maps with monsters.

​⛏️ Mining & Combat

​The Mines: A 120-floor subterranean system filled with ores (copper, iron, gold, iridium), gemstones, and hostile monsters.

​Combat: Simple real-time sword and weapon combat used to clear floors, gather crafting materials, and discover deeper underground locations like the Skull Cavern.

​🎣 Fishing & Foraging

​Fishing: A skill-based minigame that changes depending on the weather, season, time of day, and water body (ocean, river, mountain lake).

​Foraging: Gathering wild berries, mushrooms, and trees across the map to craft supplies and fences.

​💬 Social Life & Town Dynamics

​Pelican Town: Home to over 30 unique villagers, each with their own schedules, cutscenes, backstories, and personalities.

​Relationships: You can talk to villagers, give them gifts, participate in seasonal town festivals, and even marry one of the 12 eligible bachelors or bachelorettes.

​Roommates & Family: You can build a home, have children with a spouse, or ask Krobus (a friendly shadow monster) to move in as a roommate.

answers.ask: No look was stated - should the valley read as soft storybook countryside, or grounded rustic realism?
answers.answer: Use a soft storybook countryside look, matching the cozy farming RPG tone.

answers.ask: Is the mine a real 120 floors, or a handful of floors that repeat with depth? 120 built floors is a different build entirely.
answers.answer: Make it a real 120-floor mine, as specified, with floors progressing through the stated ore tiers and deeper areas.

answers.ask: Does each player get their own farm, or does one server share a single farm?
answers.answer: Each player gets their own farm so they can choose and develop their selected farm layout independently.

config.genre_evidence: The prompt explicitly says "build an rpg and farming simulator" and centers a persistent progression world: seasonal farming, animal production, a "120-floor" mine with ores and monsters, "real-time sword and weapon combat," crafting, exploration, and social relationships. config.addendum:
LAYOUT FEATURES for this RPG map. Build these as the actual structure of the space rather than as set dressing, keep them visually distinct from one another, and keep the whole layout legible in one view.

SHAPE OF THE SPACE - Hub and Dungeons: A safe hub feeding separate instanced combat areas entered from the overworld.

INCLUDE:
- Sanctuary Town: A settlement completely isolated from enemy AI where players restock, repair, and turn in quests.
- Resource Veins: Repeating alcoves and clearings reserved for mining seams, woodcutting stands, and herb patches.
- Ambient Population: The non-hostile characters who inhabit the space — shopkeepers, wandering crowds, ambient animals, a named figure players come to see — and the ground they occupy.
- Water Body: Standing or flowing water as a real feature of the map — a lake, river, sea, or pool — whether swum through or treated as a barrier.
- Settlement: Built-up ground at a stated density — a hamlet, a town, or a dense city block grid — rather than scattered individual buildings.
- Terrain Relief: Natural landform shaping the ground: hills, mountains, cliffs, a valley, or a canyon.
